adaptations.withheld: sacred or restricted dance: no teaching adaptations

movement_profile.arms_and_hands: Right hand rotates the khorawa sling continuously; left hand may hold a small llama figurine.
movement_profile.footwork: Alternating forward and backward trotting steps imitating the light movement of camelids.
movement_profile.formation_and_space: Two long parallel lines (men and women separated) performing synchronized group turns and figures.
movement_profile.hips_and_torso: Controlled, upright torso with gentle side-to-side sway following the trotting cadence.
movement_profile.levels_and_jumps: Ground-level trotting with light springy hops.
movement_profile.partnering: Non-contact line work guided by the group leader (qañiachu).
movement_profile.posture: Upright, energetic, mimicking an agile marching pasturage posture.

signature_moves.description: Continuous rhythmic twirling of the woven herding sling overhead or to the side.
signature_moves.name: Khorawa rotation

movement_profile.what_to_avoid: Avoid heavy, flat-footed stomping; steps should remain light and springy.

music_profile.musical_form: Strophic repeating melody sections suited for parade marching
music_profile.rhythm_pattern: Continuous light trotting beats matching rhythmic step-hopping
music_profile.sound_description: Bright altiplano brass or panpipe melodies set against a firm, marching bass drum pulse supporting continuous light stepping.
music_profile.vocal_style: Instrumental driven with occasional shouting or whistle calls

basic_steps: Light trotting steps advancing forward in line
teaching.formation: Two parallel columns (male and female lines)
teaching.level_notes: Accessible light stepping with focus on wrist coordination for sling rotation.
